posts.title: Characterization of HBM Power Consumption (ETH Zurich, NYU)
posts.summary:
Researchers at ETH Zürich and New York University published a technical paper titled “Understanding the Power Consumption of Modern High Bandwidth Memory: Experimental Analysis and Modeling Using Real HBM2 DRAM Chips.” Abstract Excerpt: “We perform the first comprehensive experimental characterization of power consumed by real HBM2 DRAM chips. Our extensive characterization yields 1) the empirical... » read more
The post Characterization of HBM Power Consumption (ETH Zurich, NYU) appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: A comprehensive study of real HBM2 DRAM chips reveals that read operations consume significantly more current than any other memory operation.
Data bus signal toggling is a major power driver, with internal bank group bus activity increasing power consumption by 29.4% compared to constant signals.
Researchers developed an optimized access pattern that increases power consumption by 23.6% over standard JEDEC-specified measurement loops, providing a new benchmark for HBM power modeling.

posts.title: Why Heat Is Becoming A Bigger Chip Design Issue
posts.summary:
Increasing complexity requires thermal, electrical, and mechanical effects to be analyzed together.
The post Why Heat Is Becoming A Bigger Chip Design Issue appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: Thermal management is becoming a primary design constraint as vertical die stacking and high-performance requirements create conflicting physics between voltage, timing, and heat.
Industry experts highlight the need for co-optimization loops that simultaneously address timing, thermal, and power integrity throughout the design process.
Future design methodologies will require dynamic, temperature-based transient analysis, as resistance changes with heat directly impact performance and power budgets.

posts.title: Simulations Pinpoint Leakage Pathway In GAAFETs (Sandia, Luxembourg)
posts.summary:
Researchers at Sandia National Laboratories and Luxembourg Institute of Science and Technology published a technical paper titled “Revealing New Leakage Paths in GAAFETs using Predictive First-Principles Simulations.” Abstract Excerpt: “Gate-All-Around Field-Effect Transistors (GAAFETs) are emerging as successors to Fin Field-Effect Transistors (FinFETs) and are central to continued scaling at advanced semiconductor nodes. Despite their improved... » read more
The post Simulations Pinpoint Leakage Pathway In GAAFETs (Sandia, Luxembourg) appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: Researchers identified a specific leakage pathway in Gate-All-Around FETs (GAAFETs) where drain current deviates from thermionic behavior at negative gate voltages.
The study attributes this leakage to direct gate-drain tunneling through the high-k dielectric, exacerbated by drain-induced dielectric barrier lowering (DIDBL).
Using predictive Non-Equilibrium Green Function (NEGF) simulations, the team successfully resolved the spatial origin of this leakage, providing critical data for future GAAFET scaling.

posts.title: China NEV retail sales fall 13% in October 1-11 as penetration slips to 61.2%
posts.summary:
NEV retail penetration in October 1-11 was below September's 67.0%, while wholesale penetration rose to 78.1%.
For details, please visit CnEVPost (cnev.co).
bullets: China's NEV retail sales dropped 13% year-on-year to 281,000 units during the first 11 days of October, signaling a persistent slowdown in consumer demand.
NEV retail penetration fell to 61.2% in early October, down from the record 67.0% observed in September.
Wholesale performance remained more resilient than retail, with a 6% year-on-year increase to 301,000 units, largely supported by strong export activity.
Total passenger vehicle retail sales in China declined 24% year-on-year for the same period, reflecting broader market weakness across both internal combustion and electric segments.

posts.title: The Download: faking blood and the future of batteries
posts.summary: This is today’s edition of The Download, our weekday newsletter that provides a daily dose of what’s going on in the world of technology. The US military’s race to make fake blood In February 2007, a US military helicopter carrying blood to a field hospital was shot down in Iraq, killing all seven crew members.…
bullets: DARPA has initiated a $73 million project to develop shelf-stable synthetic blood products, including plasma, platelets, and red blood cells, with a deployment target of 2029.

The initiative aims to mitigate the logistical risks and supply shortages associated with traditional blood transport, which currently causes significant preventable mortality in battlefield and trauma scenarios.
WeLion New Energy is advancing liquid-solid hybrid battery technology, building on its 2023 collaboration with Nio to deliver EV battery packs capable of exceeding 1,000 kilometers of range.
While WeLion's technology promises higher energy density and improved safety, the company faces significant commercial hurdles regarding production scalability and cost competitiveness.
